problems.stem: Which of these is an animal?
Which of these is an action word?
Which of these is an action word you can do?

problems.question: Which of these is an animal?
problems.rationale: A cat is an animal, which is a living noun. A ball is a toy and an apple is a fruit to eat, so they are not animals.
problems.teachingNote: Reinforce that nouns name people, places, things, or animals. Asking students whether a noun is alive can help them identify animal nouns.
successCriteria: Identify an animal from a set of common concrete nouns
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.question: Which of these is an action word?
problems.rationale: An action word tells something you can do, and you can run with your legs! A dog is an animal and a bed is a thing, so they are naming words instead of actions.
problems.teachingNote: Have students act out words to test whether they are verbs: if they can do it with their body, it is an action word.
successCriteria: Identify an action word (verb) from everyday words
Distinguish between an action and a person, animal, or thing
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.question: Which of these is an action word you can do?
problems.rationale: Sleeping is an action verb because it is something you can do. A bed and a hat are things you can touch, which makes them naming words or nouns. When we rest our bodies and close our eyes, we are doing the action of sleeping!
problems.teachingNote: Remind kindergarteners that verbs are 'doing words' or actions our bodies can do, while nouns are people, places, or things.
successCriteria: Identify an action verb from a set of simple words
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS
